paragraphs.text: matra parses English text into sections, paragraphs, sentences and words, and returns measures, summaries and keyphrases over them, from Rust, Python or the command line.
Install matra, save one sentence, and run matra on it.
It prints JSON; here is the first word:
Every word, drawn. Each arc runs from a word to the word that depends on it:
Tutorial: run matra on two short paragraphs and find each part of what it returns. About ten minutes.
How-to guides: one task each on real texts: summarize a document, extract keyphrases, find negations and modals, compare readability, cluster sentences by meaning.
Explanation: why the output has the shape it has, with figures you can step through.
Reference: every type and field, the Rust, Python and command-line surfaces, the methods behind each measure, and every error.
